title: English Language Paper 2 Writing – Mock Paper 2
instructions: This paper consists of two parts, Part A and Part B. Answer Question 1 in Part A and ONE question from Part B.
Part A: write about 200 words. Part B: write about 400 words.
Do not use your real name. If you need a name, use 'Chris Wong'.
You may use the information given in a question, but do not simply copy it.

partA.role: a local resident who often takes a younger brother to the playground
partA.audience: the District Officer of Pak Ling District Office
partA.prompt:
You are Chris Wong, a resident of Pak Ling Estate. You often take your younger brother to Ming Tak Road Playground, but several facilities there have been broken for weeks. You made the sketch map below, with notes on the problems.

Write a letter to the District Officer of Pak Ling District Office. In your letter, you should:
contentPoints: describe the problems and explain why they are dangerous
explain how the problems are affecting local families
suggest what should be done now and in the longer term

input.description: A hand-drawn map of a small rectangular playground. The entrance gate is at the bottom left on Ming Tak Road, with a lamp post beside it. Inside are a two-seat swing set, a slide, a climbing frame on a rubber mat, a drinking fountain and two benches. Each item has a handwritten note beside it with an arrow; broken items are circled in red. Three extra notes are written along the bottom of the page.
items: Heading: Ming Tak Road Playground – my sketch (Chris Wong)
Lamp post by the entrance gate: light not working since mid-October – playground very dark after 6:30 pm
Swing set (2 seats): left seat's chain snapped, seat hanging from one chain – residents have tied red tape round it
Slide: crack along the bottom edge – sharp piece of plastic sticking out
Climbing frame: rubber safety mat underneath torn – hole about 30 cm wide; a child tripped here on 28 October
Note: kindergarten next door brings about 20 children here on weekday mornings
Note: reported the faults on 20 October using the phone number on the playground notice board – told it would be 'followed up'; nothing done yet
Note: nearest other playground is 15 minutes' walk away, across a busy road

partB.audience: the editor and readers of The Harbourside Courier
partB.prompt: Inter-school sports competitions in Hong Kong are taken seriously, and some teams train every day. In a letter to The Harbourside Courier, a parent argued that matches for students under 15 should not keep scores at all, as the pressure to win spoils the fun. Write a letter to the editor saying whether you agree or disagree with the parent, and why.

partB.role: a candidate for Student Union president
partB.audience: the principal, teachers and fellow students at an election assembly
partB.prompt: Your school's Student Union election will be held next week. You are standing for president, and each candidate will give a speech to the whole school in the school hall. Write your speech, explaining what you would change in the school and why your fellow students should vote for you.

partB.role: a secondary school student writing for a youth magazine
partB.audience: teenage readers of the youth magazine Teen Junction
partB.prompt: Many secondary students in Hong Kong now earn money while still at school, for example by selling handmade goods online or giving lessons to younger children. Write an article for the youth magazine Teen Junction discussing the benefits and risks of running a small business while you are a secondary student.

partB.audience: judges and readers of a youth short story competition
partB.prompt: Lantern Bay Youth Library is holding a short story competition for teenagers. Your story must begin with this sentence: 'The notebook had been left on the back seat of the minibus, and nobody else seemed to have noticed it.' Write your story for the competition.
